title: Improve test coverage for bus_taps_test - add cleanup
description:
**Severity: LOW**

**File**: `core/controlplane/gateway/bus_taps_test.go:62-63`

**Issue**: Test calls `s.startBusTaps()` but never properly unsubscribes/stops the bus tap goroutines. Only closes `eventsCh`. This leaks goroutines in tests and may cause interference between test cases.

**Fix**: Add proper shutdown of bus subscriptions in test cleanup (e.g. via `t.Cleanup` or deferred stop call). Ensure no goroutine leaks after tests complete.
definitionOfDone: Tests properly clean up bus tap goroutines via t.Cleanup or defer
No goroutine leaks detectable with goleak or -race

implementationPlan.description:
The broadcast goroutine (gateway.go:723-760) already exits when `eventsCh` is closed, which the test handles via `t.Cleanup`. The real gap is that `startBusTaps` doesn't return or store subscription handles, so bus subscriptions can't be unsubscribed. In tests, the `stubBus` is synchronous (no background goroutines), so there's no actual goroutine leak from subscriptions — the only goroutine is the broadcast loop, which is properly cleaned up.

**Minimal fix**: Add a `stopBusTaps()` method to `server` that closes `eventsCh` (moving responsibility from the caller). In the test, use `t.Cleanup(s.stopBusTaps)` instead of manually closing the channel.
Add `stopBusTaps` method to `server` struct: close `eventsCh` with a `sync.Once` guard to prevent double-close panics. This also addresses the broadcast goroutine shutdown cleanly.
Update bus_taps_test.go line 63: replace `t.Cleanup(func() { close(s.eventsCh) })` with `t.Cleanup(s.stopBusTaps)` to use the new idempotent shutdown method.
Run `go test -race -count=5 ./core/controlplane/gateway/...` to verify no races or goroutine leaks.
